Rationalize and equate real/imaginary parts:

\[
\frac{a}{1-i}=\frac{a(1+i)}{2}=\frac a2+\frac a2 i,\qquad
\frac{b}{2-i}=\frac{b(2+i)}{5}=\frac{2b}{5}+\frac b5 i
\]
\[
\frac{1}{3-i}=\frac{3+i}{10}=\frac{3}{10}+\frac{1}{10}i
\]

So
\[
\frac a2+\frac{2b}{5}=\frac{3}{10},\qquad \frac a2+\frac b5=\frac{1}{10}.
\]
Solving gives \(a=-\frac15\), \(b=1\).

The sequence is \(a n+b=-\frac15 n+1\). First term \(a+b=\frac45\), common difference \(a=-\frac15\).

\[
S_{100}=\frac{100}{2}\left[2\cdot \frac45 + 99\left(-\frac15\right)\right]
=50\left(\frac85-\frac{99}{5}\right)
=50\left(-\frac{91}{5}\right)=-910.
\]

\[
\boxed{-910}
\]
